concerns.text: T032b mandates a hard failure if `data/raw/multabench_baselines.csv` is missing, yet the spec and plan explicitly state this file has no public URL and relies on 'local user setup'. This creates a deadlock violating Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) on a fresh CI runner, as the task provides no mechanism to acquire the data, effectively weakening the requirement to run on standard infrastructure.

T041 introduces 'adaptive batching' with '[deferred]' thresholds (e.g., 'Reduce batch size by [deferred] if memory > 6GB'). This violates the 'Reproducibility' principle (Constitution I) and FR-004 by introducing non-deterministic execution paths dependent on runtime conditions rather than fixed, reproducible parameters. The task weakens the deterministic constraint of the spec.

T033 specifies running correlation on '**ALL available datasets with complete data**', whereas Spec US-003 Acceptance Scenario 1 explicitly limits the analysis to the 'first 20 available datasets (alphabetically)' (or all if fewer). This silently relaxes the research design constraint, potentially altering the statistical power and scope defined in the spec.

T032a generates `gpu_tuned_baselines.csv` by validating baselines, but T032b then re-fetches baselines from the local `data/raw/multabench_baselines.csv` instead of consuming T032a's output. This violates Constitution Principle IV (Single Source of Truth) by creating a circular/conflicting data flow where the validated artifact is ignored in favor of the raw source, weakening the data integrity guarantee.

T019d trains a classifier on frozen embeddings to generate 'Frozen Baseline Performance Metrics'. However, FR-001 requires the 'Frozen Baseline' denominator to be re-computed using the *same* preprocessing steps as the 'CPU-Conditioned' generation (US2). T019d creates a separate metric stream that may not align with US2's specific preprocessing, risking a mismatch in the Recovery Ratio calculation defined in T031 and violating FR-001's consistency requirement.
